title: More blessed to give (Acts 20:17–38)
hook: Paul's tearful farewell, quoting Jesus: it is more blessed to give than to receive
tomorrow: a prophet ties himself up with Paul's own belt. why?

segments.voice: Eutychus falls asleep, falls from a window, and the room goes home not a little comforted. Paul sails on in a hurry now, and sends for old friends to meet him by the sea.
screen: `NOT A LITTLE COMFORTED.` → `OLD FRIENDS, BY THE SEA.`

segments.voice: Some goodbyes come with a speech: a graduation, a retirement party, an airport gate. Paul's comes at Miletus, a harbor town, with a ship waiting. He's hurrying toward Jerusalem, so he sends for the elders of the church at Ephesus, and tells them he doesn't expect to see their faces again. And his last words to them aren't his own. "Remember the words of the Lord Jesus, how he said, It is more blessed to give than to receive."
screen: `A GOODBYE WITH A SPEECH.` → `ELDERS AT MILETUS.` → `THE WORDS OF THE LORD JESUS.`

segments.voice: Paul sets those words inside his own life. "I have coveted no man's silver, or gold, or apparel." He holds up his hands: "these hands have ministered unto my necessities, and to them that were with me." He worked, and what he earned fed others too. Then the goodbye: "He kneeled down, and prayed with them all. And they all wept sore, and fell on Paul's neck, and kissed him." Then they walk him to the ship. So what does more blessed to give ask of people? Christians hold two honest emphases. The first: be the giver. Paul worked so he'd burden no one, and the giver's place is the blessed one. Give first, give quietly, and don't lean on others if you can help it. The second: don't make receiving shameful. Paul received too. He wrote to the Philippians that their gift to him was "an odour of a sweet smell, a sacrifice acceptable, wellpleasing to God." And when Peter refused to let Jesus wash his feet, Jesus said, "If I wash thee not, thou hast no part with me." The best case for this side: if giving is more blessed, letting someone give hands them the blessed part. Here's the one to tell a friend: the man who spoke these words of Jesus also said thank you for a gift.
screen: `THESE HANDS MINISTERED.` · `THEY FELL ON PAUL'S NECK.` · `VIEW ONE: BE THE GIVER.` · `VIEW TWO: RECEIVE WELL TOO.` · then, large: `MORE BLESSED TO GIVE.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind someone who'd never ask you for anything. Send them one small offer they didn't ask for: a ride, a hand with something heavy, a coffee on you. If you pray, you can pray for them as it sends; if not, just picture their face when they read it.
More blessed to give. Words of the Lord Jesus, handed on by Paul at a tearful goodbye, with working hands behind them.
Keep this one: more blessed to give, from a man who also knew how to say thank you. Go gently.

howItsDone: Christians quote Acts 20:35 when they collect gifts for people in need, and some churches read it when the offering is taken.

fork.setup: after your mom's surgery, a friend's family brings dinner every night. your mom hates feeling like a burden and wants to ask them to stop. what's the best case for saying yes?
options: letting them give hands them the blessed part; Paul received gladly too.
accepting help shows people you can't cope on your own.
Jesus said receiving is more blessed than giving.
fork.reveal: that's the receive-well view at its best. the give-first view answers with Paul's working hands. both are Christian voices.

original.note: Greek: blessed, in Acts 20:35, it is more blessed to give than to receive.

trapdoor: what you thought: more blessed to give is an old proverb with no clear source.
what it means: Paul hands it on as the words of the Lord Jesus, to teach the elders to support the weak.
what a scholar hears: Paul frames the saying with his own working hands, and elsewhere thanks the Philippians for a gift, so giving and receiving sit side by side in his letters.
guess: Jesus' words: giving brings more blessing
a rule that every gift must be given in secret
a promise that givers will be repaid double

chat.says: pop slipped me gas money for the audition trip. he's on a fixed income!! do i give it back?
options: Maybe let him give. More blessed to give: let Pop have that part, and thank him like you mean it.
Give it back. More blessed to give means it's wrong for you to take anything from anyone.
Keep it and don't mention it. Paul said receiving is every bit as blessed as giving.
chat.meaning: Paul handed on Jesus' words, more blessed to give, and still thanked the Philippians for their gift. Receiving well lets the giver give.

Miletus.meaning: a port town where Paul met the Ephesian elders

Philippians.meaning: the believers at Philippi, who sent Paul a gift
